Fit the outcome models for an estimand

Source: R/fit.R
pollin_fit.Rd

Fits one generalised linear mixed model per response in the estimand's data, with the pollination treatment as the fixed effect and the random terms of the design: response ~ treatment + <design random terms>. With by, the fixed part is treatment * by, so the treatment effect has its own fixed estimate at each level of by. The treatment is releveled so the estimand's low arm is the reference level. Every treatment level in the data is kept in the fit; the contrast is read from the fitted model by pollin_effects().

Usage

pollin_fit(
  estimand,
  engine = "glmmTMB",
  family = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  pooled = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

estimand

A pollin_estimand() object.

engine

The fitting engine: "glmmTMB" (the default) or "flexyBayes", a Bayesian fit on INLA through flexyBayes (see Details). On designs with a random treatment slope and few units (12 sites tested), its 95% posterior intervals cover about 91% to 93%, as an exact posterior does on those designs.

family

NULL (the default) chooses a family per response from its values (count, proportion in (0, 1), positive continuous, or continuous with zeros), or binomial() when the data declare a denominator. A single glmmTMB family object applies to every response; a named list gives one per response, and responses it does not name are chosen as for NULL. With a denominator, a family other than binomial is an error.

by

Optional name of a column of the data (for example variety or region). The treatment effect is fitted separately at each of its levels, as an interaction, and pollin_effects() then reports one contrast per level. The column is treated as a factor. An estimand whose population is a pollin_population() must be fitted with by set to the population's by column.

pooled

Optional name of a column of the data that is not a unit column (for example variety). Its levels get a random intercept and a random treatment slope, so the treatment effect at each level is pooled towards the overall effect; pollin_cate() reads the per-level effects. It must differ from by. A slope on a unit column is declared with pollin_design(slope = ) instead. Rows with a missing value in the column are dropped.

...

Passed to glmmTMB::glmmTMB(), or to flexyBayes::flexybayes() on the flexyBayes engine (for example prior or seed).

Value

An object of class pollin_fit: a list holding the estimand, the engine, the fitted models fits (named by response), the model data for each response, the right-hand-side terms rhs, the families (as glmmTMB family objects on both engines), the by column (or NULL), the denominator column (or NULL), and the further fitting arguments args.

Details

Rows with a missing value in the response, the treatment, a unit column, the denominator or the by column are dropped for that response's model.

When the data declare a denominator (pollin_data(denominator = )), each response is a count of successes out of that many trials and is fitted as binomial with a logit link, cbind(response, denominator - response) on glmmTMB. The arm means read by pollin_effects() and pollin_draws() are then expected proportions, averaged over the rows with equal weight.

With engine = "flexyBayes" each response is fitted by flexyBayes::flexybayes(backend = "inla"), which needs the flexyBayes and INLA packages. The fixed part is that of the glmmTMB engine. Each unit level is a random intercept; a nested level enters as one grouping column pollin_<outer>_<inner> added to the model data. flexyBayes fits a correlated random slope on brms only, so on INLA the treatment slope of the design is a random intercept per unit plus an independent effect per unit-by-arm cell (column pollin_<unit>_<treatment>): equal variances across arms and a non-negative correlation between them, the exchangeable form of the slope. A pooled column enters the same way. The families map as nbinom2() to "negative_binomial", poisson() to "poisson", binomial() to "binomial", Gamma(link = "log") to "gamma" and beta_family() to "beta"; any other family is refused. With a denominator, flexyBayes takes a binomial response as one 0/1 row per trial, so each row is expanded to as many rows as its denominator, its successes coded 1 and the rest 0; the arm means are still averaged over the original rows. An expansion beyond two million rows is an error, and such data are fitted with the glmmTMB engine. Priors are passed through ... as flexybayes() takes them; the seed of the posterior draws is set in pollin_draws(). The backend is INLA only, since the posterior draws of a brms fit are not in the flexyBayes extension API version 1. A fit whose convergence verdict (flexyBayes::fb_convergence()) is FALSE is an error, and one with no verdict a warning. Estimates and intervals of a flexyBayes fit come from its posterior draws; see pollin_draws().

See also

pollin_effects() for estimates and intervals on the estimand's scale.

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(
  trt = rep(rep(c("Cage", "Open"), each = 10L), 8L),
  Site = rep(paste0("s", seq_len(8L)), each = 20L)
)
d$pods <- rnbinom(nrow(d), mu = exp(3 + 0.3 * (d$trt == "Open")), size = 10)
pd <- pollin_data(d, "pods", "trt", unit = "Site")
ds <- pollin_design(pd, c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"), "rcbd")
est <- pollin_estimand(ds, "dependence", "ratio", "loss")
pollin_fit(est)
#> <pollin_fit>
#>   engine    : glmmTMB 
#>   family    : dependence 
#>   contrast  : Open vs Cage 
#>   model     : <response> ~ trt + (1 | Site) 
#>   pods      : nbinom2, 160 rows
# }
